transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been having terrible trouble sleeping and feel completely exhausted. Ever since a really scary event about two weeks ago, I can't seem to rest and my mind is constantly flooded with disturbing memories. I just don't know what to do anymore.
I am so sorry to hear you're going through this. To help me understand better, could you tell me a little bit more about what happened during that scary event two weeks ago?
It is really hard for me to talk about what happened, and I'd prefer not to go into the details of the event itself right now. Just thinking about it makes me feel completely overwhelmed.
I completely understand and respect that. Without going into the details of what happened, did you feel that your life or physical safety was in immediate danger during that event?
It's really hard to say, and I don't really want to think about it enough to answer that. Just trying to look back at how I felt in that moment makes me feel very uneasy.

I completely understand, and we do not have to talk about the event itself. Since it happened, have you noticed yourself feeling constantly on edge, unusually jumpy, or extra watchful of your surroundings?
No, I haven't really noticed feeling constantly on edge, jumpy, or extra watchful of my surroundings. My main struggle is just being completely exhausted and unable to get any proper rest.
Since the event, have you felt emotionally numb, or experienced a strange sense that you or your surroundings aren't quite real?
No, I haven't felt emotionally numb, and I haven't had any feelings that I or my surroundings aren't real. Everything feels very real, it's just that my mind won't let me rest.
Since the event, have you been actively trying to avoid certain places, people, conversations, or situations that might remind you of what happened?

Yes, I've been doing everything I can to avoid certain places and people that remind me of what happened. I also try to steer clear of any conversations or situations that might bring those memories back. It just feels easier to stay away from anything related to it.
Since the event occurred, have you found it difficult to experience positive feelings, like happiness, joy, or love?
I haven't really noticed if I'm having trouble feeling positive emotions. I've been so consumed by my constant sleep issues and those distressing memories that I haven't really thought about it.
Since the event, have you found it harder than usual to concentrate or focus on your daily tasks or work?

I haven't really noticed any major issues with my concentration or focus specifically. I'm not really sure about that, as my main struggle has just been trying to get through the day while being so exhausted.
Since the event, have you had any distressing dreams or nightmares related to what happened?
Yes, I've been having awful nightmares and distressing dreams that are directly related to what happened. They wake me up constantly and make it impossible to get any restful sleep.
Since the event, have you had moments where you suddenly feel or act as if the scary event is actually happening all over again?

Yes, I frequently have those moments, and they are absolutely terrifying. It feels like I am suddenly pulled right back into the event, reacting as if it is happening all over again in real time. It is so incredibly vivid and distressing that it completely overwhelms me.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports experiencing a highly traumatic event two weeks ago, followed by intrusive memories, nightmares, flashbacks, avoidance of reminders, and sleep disturbance. Because the symptoms have lasted for two weeks (less than the one month required for PTSD), the primary differentials are Acute Stress Disorder and Adjustment Disorder. Further evaluation is needed to determine if the symptom criteria for Acute Stress Disorder (at least 9 symptoms across intrusion, negative mood, dissociation, avoidance, and arousal) are fully met, or if Adjustment Disorder is the more appropriate diagnosis.
